issue.title: Expose MCP server health via Spring Boot Actuator
issue.body:
## Problem

Applications using `embabel-agent-starter-mcpserver` have no operational health signal beyond the `helloBanner` MCP tool. Platform operators running Embabel as an MCP server (Docker, Kubernetes, enterprise gateways) cannot easily answer:

- Is the MCP server initialized and serving tools?
- How many tools are registered?
- Is the server in SYNC or ASYNC mode?
- Are there initialization issues?

This is especially painful alongside #1557 (graceful shutdown): ops teams need both **liveness/readiness** and **clean shutdown**.

## Observation

`ServerHealthStatus` already exists in `embabel-agent-mcpserver` with unit tests, but is not wired to any runtime health check:

- `com.embabel.agent.mcpserver.domain.ServerHealthStatus`
- `ToolRegistry` already exposes `getToolCount()` / `getToolNames()`

There is currently no `HealthIndicator` / `HealthContributor` in the repository.

## Proposed solution

When `spring-boot-starter-actuator` is on the classpath and MCP server is enabled:

1. Register an `McpServerHealthIndicator` (name TBD) that builds `ServerHealthStatus` from:
   - execution mode (`SYNC` / `ASYNC`)
   - registered tool count (and optionally tool names in details)
   - initialization state (server strategy initialized vs still starting)
   - any collected issues (e.g. zero tools exported when agents are expected)

2. Expose details under Actuator health (e.g. `/actuator/health` component `mcpServer`).

3. Optional: `embabel.agent.mcpserver.health.min-tools` property to mark health `DOWN` when tool count is below threshold (useful for readiness probes).

4. Document in `reference/integrations/page.adoc` with K8s readiness/liveness example.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `McpServerHealthIndicator` returns `UP` when MCP server is initialized with expected tools
- [ ] Health details include `mode`, `toolCount`, `timestamp`, and `issues` (matching `ServerHealthStatus`)
- [ ] Indicator is conditional on Actuator + MCP server enabled (no hard dependency on Actuator in mcpserver starter)
- [ ] Unit tests for healthy / unhealthy / not-initialized states
- [ ] Integration test with `@SpringBootTest` + Actuator (if pattern exists in repo)
- [ ] Documentation updated

## Motivation / context

I'm building enterprise agent platforms (multi-tenant Spring AI gateway, MCP tooling) and need standard Actuator health for MCP-enabled Embabel services—the same way we expose `/api/health` for other platform services. Happy to contribute a PR if this direction looks right.

## Related

- #1557 — MCP server graceful shutdown
- `helloBanner` tool (client-facing, not ops-facing)

issue.title: VictoolsSchemaGenerator does not honor nested Jackson annotations for parameter serialization
InMemoryContentChunker returns chunks longer than maxChunkSize
issue.body:
`InMemoryContentChunker.chunk()` checks whether a section fits in one chunk by adding up each leaf's title and content. The chunk it then builds puts a blank line (`"\n\n"`) between leaves, and the check doesn't count those. So a section just over the limit comes back as one chunk longer than `maxChunkSize`, which `ContentChunker.Config` documents as the "Maximum size of each chunk in characters".

```kotlin
val document = MaterializedDocument(
    id = "document",
    title = "Document",
    children = listOf("A", "B", "C").map { LeafSection(id = it, title = it, text = "abc") },
    uri = "test",
)
InMemoryContentChunker(ContentChunker.Config(maxChunkSize = 15, overlapSize = 0))
    .chunk(document)
    .map { it.text.length }   // [19]
```

The check counts 15 characters (three leaves of `title + "\n" + "abc"`), and the chunk is `A\nabc\n\nB\nabc\n\nC\nabc`, 19 characters.

The overshoot is up to 2 characters for each leaf after the first: a few characters for a section with a handful of leaves, 18 for a section of 10 titled leaves. Documents are chunked this way on ingestion: `AbstractChunkingContentElementRepository.writeAndChunkDocument()` creates this chunker from its config, and `LuceneSearchOperations` extends that repository.

`groupLeavesForOptimalChunking()`, used when a section doesn't fit, already adds 2 per separator. Only the single-chunk check leaves them out.

I have a small fix and a regression test, and will open a PR for it.

issue.title: Claude 5: keep thinking across tool calls
issue.body:
🤖 Claude 5 (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5) thinks by default. In an Embabel tool loop, the reasoning from one model call is currently dropped before the next call. This issue tracks keeping it.

## Problem

Anthropic checks the prefix of a conversation in which a model thought ([preserved thinking, prefix check](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#prefix-check)). It accepts an earlier turn's thinking only when that turn, and everything before it, goes back exactly as Claude produced it. Any edit gets a 400. The prefix covers the system prompt, the tools and every earlier message. Leaving thinking out of earlier turns is allowed.

Spring AI 2.0.1's `AnthropicChatModel` cannot send a turn back as it was produced. It rebuilds an assistant turn from its joined text, its thinking blocks and its tool calls, in that order. So a returned `[thinking, text, tool_use]` goes back as `[text, thinking, tool_use]`. A turn with `[thinking A, tool_use a, thinking B, tool_use b]` goes back as `[thinking A, thinking B, tool_use a, tool_use b]`, and consecutive text blocks are merged into one.

## Current behaviour (#2119)

[embabel/embabel-agent#2119](https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/pull/2119) leaves Anthropic's thinking out of every earlier assistant turn. It does this when converting history for Spring AI (`messageConverters.kt`), and blocking and streaming calls share that conversion. Requests succeed. The model loses its reasoning across tool calls, which Anthropic recommends keeping.

## Design options

1. **Replay at the HTTP layer.** An anthropic-java `Interceptor` on the factory's clients records each tool-calling response's `content`, keyed by `tool_use` ids. It puts that content back in place of Spring AI's rebuild. It keeps thinking only when the turn is provably unchanged:
   - the turn is recorded;
   - its text, tool calls and thinking all match the rebuild, so a `ToolLoopTransformer`'s edits still go out as edited;
   - a digest of the system prompt, tools and earlier messages matches, ignoring Anthropic's `cache_control` marker positions.

   Anything unproven loses its thinking, and every earlier turn's, with a warning. A prototype exists: about 200 lines plus about 15 wire tests, on an unpublished branch. It covers streaming only when the factory also supplies Spring AI's async client, and that change also fixes a separate defect: today streamed BYOK calls read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` instead of the factory's key and base URL. Limits: records live in memory per client, so a restart, an eviction or a streamed response loses the reasoning. Review found three classes of bugs in this approach; each was fixed, but the surface is wide. Those classes were transformer edits silently undone, edits to tool schemas hidden from the digest, and lost HTTP observations.
2. **Anthropic's own mismatch handling.** The beta `prefix_mismatch_behavior: drop_block` makes the API drop mismatched thinking blocks instead of failing, and `tool_addition` blocks cover tools added mid-loop. This is less code, but it needs beta headers, verification per model and gateway, and behaviour that depends on the provider. It does not fix Spring AI's reordering; it only makes the reordering non-fatal.
3. **A tool-loop message model that carries provider content blocks in order.** This is the direction of #1716. Assistant messages would keep the provider's blocks (thinking, text, tool use) in the order they were produced, and the provider adapter would send them back verbatim. This removes the need for interception and recording, and keeps thinking across restarts if history is persisted. It needs either Spring AI to keep block order or Embabel to build Anthropic requests itself.

## Streaming

- **Blocking and streaming are the same.** `SpringAiLlmMessageStreamer` collects the stream with Spring AI's `MessageAggregator`. The final assistant message carries the same thinking contents as a blocking response, and goes through the same `toSpringAiMessage` conversion. So the drop in #2119 applies to both, and so would options 2 and 3.
- **Option 1 can't keep streamed thinking.** It cannot record a streamed response without buffering the server-sent events, so streamed turns would always lose their thinking.
- **Streaming needs the factory's own async client.** Today Spring AI builds the streaming client itself. Building it from the factory, with Spring AI's `AnthropicSetup` on the factory's `ObservationRegistry` so HTTP observations survive, is needed for any interception and fixes the BYOK defect above.

## Related

- #1716: native thinking content in blocking and streaming calls.
- #2119: catalogue and Claude 5 support, which drops thinking from earlier turns.

issue.title: Tool failures surface as normal string results over MCP — `CallToolResult.isError` never set
issue.body:
`SpringToolCallbackAdapter.call` maps both `Tool.Result.Error` and thrown exceptions to a
plain string (`SpringToolCallbackAdapter.kt:64-80`):

```kotlin
is Tool.Result.Error -> {
    logger.warn("Tool '{}' returned error: {}", tool.definition.name, result.message)
    "ERROR: ${result.message}"
}
...
} catch (e: Exception) {
    logger.error("Tool '{}' threw exception: {}", tool.definition.name, e.message, e)
    "ERROR: ${e.message ?: "Unknown error"}"
}
```

Spring AI's MCP wrapping (`McpToolUtils.toSyncToolSpecification`) only sets
`isError = true` when the `ToolCallback` throws. Since the adapter never lets anything
escape, every tool failure reaches the client as a successful `tools/call` response whose
text happens to start with `ERROR:` — `CallToolResult.isError` is `false`.

A client or agent harness cannot programmatically distinguish "the tool answered" from
"the tool failed / was denied". Access-control denials (`AccessDeniedException` thrown
inside a tool body, e.g. via `@SecureAgentTool`) are indistinguishable at the protocol
level from a successful answer that mentions an error. Clients that branch on `isError`
(retries, fallback tools, error rendering) misbehave, and tests are forced to assert on
error string shapes instead of the protocol flag.

## Repro

Passing test that documents the current behavior end to end through Spring AI's MCP
wrapping (`spring-ai-mcp` and mockk are already on `embabel-agent-api`'s test classpath):

```kotlin
class ToolErrorMcpMappingTest {

    class ThrowingTool : Tool {
        override val definition = object : Tool.Definition {
            override val name = "boom"
            override val description = "always throws"
            override val inputSchema = object : Tool.InputSchema {
                override fun toJsonSchema() = """{"type":"object","properties":{}}"""
                override val parameters = emptyList<Tool.Parameter>()
            }
        }
        override val metadata = object : Tool.Metadata {
            override val returnDirect = false
            override val providerMetadata = emptyMap<String, Any>()
        }

        override fun call(input: String): Tool.Result = throw IllegalStateException("access denied")
    }

    @Test
    fun `thrown exception becomes a non-error MCP result`() {
        val callback = SpringToolCallbackAdapter(ThrowingTool())

        // The adapter swallows the exception into a plain string
        assertEquals("ERROR: access denied", callback.call("{}"))

        // So Spring AI's MCP wrapping never flags the result as an error
        val spec = McpToolUtils.toSyncToolSpecification(callback)
        val exchange = mockk<McpSyncServerExchange>(relaxed = true)
        val request = McpSchema.CallToolRequest.builder().name("boom").arguments(emptyMap<String, Any>()).build()
        val result = spec.callHandler().apply(exchange, request)

        assertNotEquals(true, result.isError)  // should be true
        assertEquals("ERROR: access denied", (result.content().first() as McpSchema.TextContent).text())
    }
}
```

Also reproduces against a real MCP SDK client over both SSE and streamable-HTTP
transports: WARN `Tool 'x' returned error: …` in the server log, normal-looking string
result on the wire.

## Not fixed by upgrading

Spring AI 2.0.0's `McpToolUtils` has the same contract as 1.1.7 — `isError(true)` only in
the catch path
(https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/v2.0.0/mcp/common/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/mcp/McpToolUtils.java#L266-L278).
The swallowing happens in this repo's adapter, so no Spring / Spring Boot / Spring AI
upgrade changes the wire behavior.

## Suggested fix

Either let failures propagate out of the adapter (Spring AI's MCP wrapping then sets
`isError = true` with the message as content), or map `Tool.Result.Error` and exceptions
to a protocol-level error explicitly. Security-relevant exceptions
(`AccessDeniedException`, `AuthenticationException`) should arguably always be
protocol-level errors.

## Open questions

- `SpringToolCallbackAdapter` also serves the LLM tool-loop path, where returning the
  error message to the model as an ordinary result is often the desired behavior. Throwing
  `ToolExecutionException` would keep that path working (Spring AI's
  `ToolExecutionExceptionProcessor` turns it back into a message result) while fixing MCP,
  but if the two paths need different mappings, the adapter may need to make it
  configurable.
- Should `Tool.Result.Error` and thrown exceptions map the same way, or is
  `Result.Error` a "soft" error that stays a normal result while exceptions become
  protocol errors?

issue.title: EntityFilter silently drops all Chunk results on the in-memory post-filter fallback
issue.body:
## Summary

When a metadata/entity-filtered search falls back to in-memory post-filtering (i.e. the store implements `VectorSearch` but **not** `FilteringVectorSearch`), an `EntityFilter` silently removes **every** `Chunk` result rather than filtering them.

## Mechanism

`PostFilteringSearch.search` (`PostFilteringStrategy.kt:115`) delegates to `InMemoryPropertyFilter.filterResults`, which applies the entity filter via `matchesObject`. That method short-circuits for any target that is not a `NamedEntityData`:

https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/blob/main/embabel-agent-rag/embabel-agent-rag-core/src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/rag/filter/InMemoryPropertyFilter.kt#L61-L72

```kotlin
fun matchesObject(filter: PropertyFilter, target: Any): Boolean {
    if (target is NamedEntityData) {
        return matchesEntity(filter, target)
    }
    return when (filter) {
        is EntityFilter -> false // Entity filters only apply to NamedEntityData
        else -> GenericPropertyFilter.matches(filter, extractProperties(target))
    }
}
```

A `Chunk` is not a `NamedEntityData`, so `EntityFilter.HasAnyLabel` (currently the only `EntityFilter` subtype) evaluates to `false` for every chunk and the result set is emptied.

## Reproduction

```java
ToolishRag rag = new ToolishRag("docs", "Product documentation", store)   // store: VectorSearch, not FilteringVectorSearch
    .withEntityFilter(EntityFilter.hasAnyLabel("Person"));
```

With the default `vectorSearchFor = [Chunk]`, both the `vectorSearch` tool and — after #1958 — eager search return zero results. No error, no warning; the caller just sees an empty result set or an empty preloaded hint.

The same applies to the `Chunk` arm when `vectorSearchFor` mixes `Chunk` and entity types: entity hits filter correctly, chunk hits are all discarded.

## Why it matters

The failure is silent and looks identical to "nothing matched your query". Stores that implement `FilteringVectorSearch` (e.g. the graph stores in `embabel-agent-rag-graph`) are unaffected, so this only bites on the fallback path — which makes it easy to miss in testing and easy to hit in production on a different store.

Note this is pre-existing behaviour on the tool path, not a regression. It is worth raising separately because #1958 routes eager search through the same fallback, widening the surface where it can be observed.

## Suggested resolution

Decide what an `EntityFilter` should mean for a non-entity result and make it explicit, rather than silently `false`. Options:

1. Treat a non-entity target as **out of scope** for the entity filter and pass it through unfiltered (filter entities, leave chunks alone).
2. Keep the current exclude semantics but `log.warn` when post-filtering drops 100% of a non-empty result set, so the cause is discoverable.
3. Reject the combination up front — throw when an `EntityFilter` is configured on a `ToolishRag` whose `vectorSearchFor`/`searchFor` contains non-entity types and the store cannot filter natively.

(1) matches the principle of least surprise; (2) is the minimum viable fix and could ship alongside either.

Found while reviewing #1958.

issue.title: The deployment default LLM cannot name a role, so BYOK still needs a restart for the first key
issue.body:
`embabel.models.default-llm` must name a model, and that name is resolved among the `LlmService` beans registered when `modelProvider` is built. Under BYOK the key arrives after startup, so on an installation that has never had one there is nothing for the name to resolve to and the default falls to the placeholder — permanently, until the process restarts.

Roles do not have this problem. #1889 gave them an SPI: a `RoleResolver` is asked per call, can answer with a `ProviderCredential`, and the service is built and cached then. An application can therefore make every role work from a key stored a second ago. The deployment default is the one thing left that cannot.

**Where this bites**

Guide, and other internal projects that follow the same pattern, ship no provider starters and take their key from first-run setup (BYOK). We have just made every role resolve against the key the application holds *now*, so connecting a provider no longer needs a restart — except the very first one on a fresh installation, purely because the default has nothing to resolve to. That is the difference between "paste a key and ask a question" and "paste a key, wait for the app to come back".

**What we would like**

Any one of these would close it; the first is the smallest.

1. **Let `default-llm` name a role.** `default-llm: workhorse` resolves through the same resolver chain as any other role, so a credential-backed installation needs nothing registered at startup. A name still works, so nothing existing changes.
2. **Fall back to the role chain when the name is not registered.** If `default-llm: gpt-4.1-mini` resolves to nothing, ask the resolvers for it as a role before handing back the placeholder.
3. **A `DefaultLlmResolver` SPI**, or `RoleResolver` being asked for a well-known role name when the default is wanted.

**What we are not asking for**

We considered doing this on the application side by registering a delegating `LlmService` under the default's name, which resolves the real service per call. It works, but it means an application implementing `com.embabel.agent.spi.LlmService` — a package the SPI's own documentation asks application code not to depend on — and an F-bounded interface whose `withKnowledgeCutoffDate`/`withPromptContributor` return the self type. A shim would also have to report a name, provider and pricing before any key exists. That is a lot of framework-shaped code in an application to work around one property that cannot name a role.

**Context**

- `ConfigurableModelProvider` takes `llms = applicationContext.getBeansOfType(LlmService::class.java).values.toList()` once, at construction, which is why late registration is invisible.
- `ConfigurableModelProviderProperties`: *"Default LLM name. Must be an LLM name."*
- The existing application-side workaround for the role half, now superseded by #1889, is a `BeanFactoryPostProcessor` that rewrites `embabel.models.llms` per provider before anything reads it. We would rather delete it than grow a second one for the default.

issue.title: Generically handle models that reject unsupported request parameters (e.g. temperature)
issue.body:
## Problem

Some OpenAI models accept only the default value for certain request parameters and return a 400 otherwise, e.g.:

> 400 Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.8 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.

This affects the whole GPT-5 family and, as of ~June 2026, also **gpt-4.1** models — the OpenAI API tightened `gpt-4.1-mini` to default-temperature-only *after* `openai-models.yml` was last verified (2026-03-29). Any agent/example that sets a non-default `temperature` on such a model fails at runtime.

The same class of problem will recur for other params (`topP`, `frequencyPenalty`, reasoning-specific options) and other providers, so it is worth solving generically rather than per-model.

## Current handling (ad hoc)

- `openai-models.yml` marks restricted models with `special_handling.supports_temperature: false`.
- `OpenAiModelsConfig` branches on that flag to pick `Gpt5ChatOptionsConverter` (omits temperature) vs `StandardOpenAiOptionsConverter` (sends it).

Limitations:
- Temperature-specific, via a dedicated converter class — doesn't generalize to other params.
- The capability table goes stale as the provider changes (exactly what happened with gpt-4.1).
- `SpringAiLlmMessageSender` re-adds `temperature` in its fallback options-builder branch, which can undo the converter's decision.

## Proposed solution (two complementary strategies)

**1. Declarative capabilities (primary).** Generalize `supports_temperature` into a small capabilities object on the model metadata, sourced from the model YAML:

```kotlin
data class ModelCapabilities(
    val supportsTemperature: Boolean = true,
    val supportsTopP: Boolean = true,
    val supportsFrequencyPenalty: Boolean = true,
    // extend as providers add restrictions
)
```

Have a single `OptionsConverter` consult it and omit unsupported params (replacing the `Gpt5ChatOptionsConverter` / `StandardOpenAiOptionsConverter` split). Ensure `SpringAiLlmMessageSender` never re-adds a param the converter dropped.

**2. Defensive retry (safety net).** In the `InstrumentedChatModel` seam, catch the provider's "unsupported value: '<param>'" 400, strip that parameter, and retry once (logged as a warning). This self-heals for restricted models not yet catalogued and for future provider changes. Scope it narrowly to the known "unsupported value" errors so it doesn't mask genuine bad requests.

Using both gives correctness-by-default **and** resilience to the provider changing underneath us.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Setting a non-default temperature on a temperature-restricted model does not 400; it is dropped with a warning.
- [ ] Mechanism is generic across parameters, not temperature-specific.
- [ ] `openai-models.yml` capability data drives behavior; gpt-4.1 + gpt-5 families marked correctly.
- [ ] Defensive retry recovers from an uncatalogued restricted model.

## Context
Surfaced during the Spring AI 2.0.0 GA migration (the `repeatuntil` example 400'd on `gpt-4.1-mini` + `temperature=0.8`). The immediate example unblock was handled separately; this issue tracks the systemic fix.

Relevant code:
- `embabel-agent-autoconfigure/models/embabel-agent-openai-autoconfigure/src/main/resources/models/openai-models.yml`
- `embabel-agent-openai/src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/openai/converters.kt`
- `embabel-agent-autoconfigure/models/embabel-agent-openai-autoconfigure/src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/config/models/openai/OpenAiModelsConfig.kt`
- `embabel-agent-api/src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/spi/support/springai/SpringAiLlmMessageSender.kt`
- `embabel-agent-api/src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/spi/support/springai/InstrumentedChatModel.kt`
